1.w: Praise the Lord, O my soul! O Lord my God, you are magnificent. You are robed in splendor and majesty.

2.w: He covers himself with light as if it were a garment. He stretches out the skies like a tent curtain

3.w: and lays the beams of the upper rooms of his palace on the rain clouds. He makes the clouds his chariot and travels on the wings of the wind.

4.w: He makes the winds his messengers and the flaming fire his attendant.

5.w: He established the earth on its foundations; it will never be moved.

6.w: The watery deep covered it like a garment; the waters reached above the mountains.

7.w: Your shout made the waters retreat; at the sound of your thunderous voice they hurried off—

8.w: as the mountains rose up and the valleys went down— to the place you appointed for them.

9.w: You set up a boundary for them that they could not cross, so that they would not cover the earth again.

10.w: He turns springs into streams; they flow between the mountains.

11.w: They provide water for all the animals in the field; the wild donkeys quench their thirst.

12.w: The birds of the sky live beside them; they chirp among the bushes.

13.w: He waters the mountains from the upper rooms of his palace; the earth is full of the fruit you cause to grow.

14.w: He provides grass for the cattle and crops for people to cultivate, so they can produce food from the ground

15.w: as well as wine that makes people glad, and olive oil to make their faces shine as well as bread that sustains them.

16.w: The trees of the Lord receive all the rain they need, the cedars of Lebanon that he planted,

17.w: where the birds make nests near the evergreens in which the herons live.

18.w: The wild goats live in the high mountains; the rock badgers find safety in the cliffs.

19.w: He made the moon to mark the months, and the sun sets according to a regular schedule.

20.w: You make it dark and night comes, during which all the beasts of the forest prowl around.

21.w: The lions roar for prey, seeking their food from God.

22.w: When the sun rises, they withdraw and sleep in their dens.

23.w: People then go out to do their work, and they labor until evening.

24.w: How many living things you have made, O Lord! You have exhibited great skill in making all of them; the earth is full of the living things you have made.

25.w: Over here is the deep, wide sea, which teems with innumerable swimming creatures, living things both small and large.

26.w: The ships travel there, and over here swims the whale you made to play in it.

27.w: All your creatures wait for you to provide them with food on a regular basis.

28.w: You give food to them and they receive it; you open your hand and they are filled with food.

29.w: When you ignore them, they panic. When you take away their life’s breath, they die and return to dust.

30.w: When you send your life-giving breath, they are created, and you replenish the surface of the ground.

31.w: May the splendor of the Lord endure. May the Lord find pleasure in the living things he has made.

32.w: He looks down on the earth and it shakes; he touches the mountains and they start to smolder.

33.w: I will sing to the Lord as long as I live; I will sing praise to my God as long as I exist.

34.w: May my thoughts be pleasing to him. I will rejoice in the Lord.

35.w: May sinners disappear from the earth, and the wicked vanish. Praise the Lord, O my soul. Praise the Lord.
